members.name: Jessica Adler
members.organization: North America Wholesale and Retail Stores, Merrell
members.bio:
Jessica Adler is Vice President of North America for Merrell, a Wolverine Worldwide brand, where she leads the company’s North American commercial business across U.S. Wholesale, Canada Wholesale, and U.S. Retail. With responsibility for the region’s growth strategy and commercial performance, Jessica brings a consumer-first mindset, strong marketplace expertise, and a track record of building high-performing teams and businesses.

Since joining Merrell, Jessica has played a key role in accelerating the brand’s growth and evolving its commercial strategy across channels. Prior to joining Merrell, she held senior leadership roles at Levi Strauss & Co., Psycho Bunny, and Diesel, building businesses and teams across a range of brands, categories, and stages of growth.

Jessica began her career in the merchandise buying program at Kohl’s Department Stores after earning her undergraduate Business degree from the University of Wisconsin–Madison.

A recipient of the 2024 “Women Who Rock” Award, Jessica is passionate about developing talent, advancing women in leadership, and creating meaningful connections across the industry.

Jessica lives in New York with her husband and 3 children. Outside of work, she enjoys traveling, entertaining, spending time with family, and staying active through tennis and Pilates.

members.name: Talicia Bashford
members.bio:
Talicia Bashford is a seasoned professional with more than two decades of experience in the insurance industry. Currently serving as the Managing Director of the Midwest for Alera Group, Talicia plays a pivotal role in integrating national resources into regional operations, ensuring clients and colleagues receive strategic and innovative solutions tailored to their needs.

With a profound understanding of the insurance marketplace, Talicia remains at the forefront of trends, alternative solutions, insurance carriers, and market conditions, establishing herself as a trusted leader in the industry.

Talicia’s journey in insurance began more than 20 years ago as a producer and team leader at the Horton Group in Orland Park, IL. She then spent nine years with Assurance, initially leading small commercial, small benefits, and personal lines, before transitioning to a senior leadership role driving strategic solutions across the company. At Assurance, Talicia’s responsibilities included overseeing technology initiatives, leading geographic expansion, driving employee culture and engagement, and helping clients recognize the financial value of working with the company, transforming insurance into an investment rather than a commodity.

Throughout her extensive career, she has also held leadership positions as a local President at AssuredPartners of Chicago and Chief Operating Officer at Associated Agencies.

Beyond her professional endeavors, Talicia contributes to the industry as a member of the Wisconsin School of Business External Advisory Board and various commercial insurance advisory boards. She has also spoken on various panels and presented on the topics of technology in the insurance industry, thinking differently about client needs, and employee engagement.

Talicia holds a double major in Risk & Insurance and Marketing from the University of Wisconsin–Madison, underpinning her expertise with a solid academic foundation. Her dedication, industry knowledge, and leadership skills continue to drive success and innovation in the insurance sector.

members.name: Nooshin Felsenthal
members.position: Managing Director, Regional Director - Central U.S. Chicago
members.bio: Nooshin Felsenthal joined Tishman Speyer in 2019 and is currently responsible for the company’s operations across the Central United States. In this role she oversees the firm’s investment, development, and asset management efforts in Chicago, Austin, Columbus, and Pittsburgh. Prior to joining Tishman Speyer, she co-led the CBD investment sales team at JLL. In her role, she specialized in disposition and recapitalization of investment real estate located in Chicago and the greater Midwest. While there, she executed in excess of 14 billion dollars of investment sales transactions. Nooshin is a member of ULI and serves on the Children’s Service Board for the Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children’s Hospital of Chicago. She holds her BBA in finance, investments, and banking from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, as well as her MBA from Northwestern University’s Kellogg School of Management.

members.name: Jay Finnane
members.bio:
I am a retired Senior Partner at EY, where I served as a Global Client Service Partner in EY’s Industrials & Energy Industry Group, advising large multinational companies and leading complex, transformative initiatives. I worked closely with clients to turn their most pressing challenges into opportunities for innovation, growth, and sustainable value across functions and geographies.

Beyond my professional career, I am passionate about education, the environment, and entrepreneurship. I continue to advance these interests through board service, strategic investments, and active engagement with organizations and initiatives that are creating meaningful, lasting impact. My personal purpose is to see and develop the best in everyone so that we can tackle our biggest challenges together—a philosophy that continues to guide how I contribute, mentor, and invest my time.

members.name: Pat Halter
members.bio:
Patrick Halter is the retired President and CEO of Principal Asset Management, a global investment management business under the Principal Financial Group.  Over a career spanning 40 years,  Halter was instrumental in transforming the firm into a premier global asset manager, notably building a team of 850 investment professionals serving clients in 80 markets and continuously recognized by Pension & Investments as “Best Places to Work in Money Management”.  He first joined Principal in 1984 in the commercial real estate division and eventually served as CEO of Principal Real Estate Investors from 2003 to 2018.  The real estate business becoming one of the largest in the world.

Beyond his corporate leadership, Halter was active in the investment industry, serving on the boards of 15 investment boutiques and the Principal Mutual fund board.  He was also a member of the Board of Governors for the Investment Company Institute and a past Chairman of the National Association of Real Estate Investment Managers (NAREIM). An alumnus of the University of Wisconsin -Madison, where he earned both a bachelors degree and a MBA in Finance.

members.name: Patrick Hammes
members.bio:
Patrick Hammes is the Chief Executive Officer of the Hammes platform.

He is responsible for strategic and operational oversight of the firm’s complementary suite of services spanning real estate consulting, development, investment, and management. He also serves as a Managing Principal and Investment Committee member of Hammes Partners.

Prior to joining Hammes in 2012, Patrick was in the Business Services and Healthcare Investment Banking Group at Robert W. Baird & Co., where he led a wide range of financial advisory transactions, including mergers and acquisitions, equity and debt offerings, valuation opinions, and private placements. Before Baird, Patrick was an attorney at the law firm Strasburger & Price (now Clark Hill) in Dallas, Texas, and previously clerked in the General Counsel’s office of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services in Washington, DC.

Patrick serves as a Board Member and Immediate Past Chair of the Board of Directors for Children’s Wisconsin, the leading pediatric health system in Wisconsin and one of the top pediatric health systems in the country.  Patrick is the First Vice Chair for the Board of Trustees of The Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Milwaukee, the largest single-city Boys & Girls Club organization in the United States.  Patrick is also a member of the Dean’s External Advisory Board for the Wisconsin School of Business, the Finance Council for the Archdiocese of Milwaukee, and the Greater Milwaukee Committee (GMC).

He holds a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science and a Master of Business Administration in corporate finance from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he was the recipient of the Wisconsin Distinguished Graduate Fellowship. He earned his J.D. from Georgetown University Law Center.

members.name: Sean Jacobsohn
members.bio:
Sean Jacobsohn is a partner at Norwest and a former enterprise cloud executive with broad technology, sales, and business development expertise. He focuses on early to late-stage investment opportunities in enterprise cloud, including mobile-first business applications, human-assisted AI, B2B marketplaces, and industry cloud solutions.

Sean was previously a venture partner at Emergence Capital Partners where he focused on enterprise cloud investments, after being an executive and advisor at Emergence Capital portfolio companies Hightail and Doximity, respectively. Previously he was VP of Channel Management at Cornerstone OnDemand (NASDAQ: CSOD), a human capital management software-as-a-service provider. Sean helped grow the company from $7 million to $75 million in revenue and 300,000 subscribers to over 7.5 million. Before his tenure at Cornerstone OnDemand, Sean was VP of Sales and Partner Development at WageWorks (NYSE: WAGE), a leading provider of consumer-directed spending solutions, which grew from $3 million to $82 million in revenue during his tenure. Prior to WageWorks, he was at Upwork (NYSE: UPWK), the world’s largest marketplace of contractors.

Sean holds an MBA from Harvard Business School and a BBA in Marketing, Finance, and International Business from the University of Wisconsin. He’s co-founder of the HBS Alumni Angels, the largest university-affiliated angel group in the world, and is the Founder, Chief Historian, and Collector for the Failure Museum.

members.name: Tim Mattke
members.bio:
Timothy J. Mattke is Chief Executive Officer of MGIC Investment Corporation and MGIC. He joined the company in 2006. Prior to his appointment as CEO, he served as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer from 2014 to 2019, our Controller from 2009 to 2014, and held other positions within the Accounting and Finance Departments. Before joining MGIC, Mr. Mattke was an Audit Manager with PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP. He has a BBA from the University of Wisconsin–Madison as well as an MA in Accountancy from that University.

Mr. Mattke currently serves on the Boards of Acts Housing, Goodwill Greater Milwaukee & Chicago and West Bend Mutual Holding Company, and sits on the Advisory Council of SecureFutures.

members.name: Adam Peck
members.bio: Adam J. Peck co-founded Riverwater Partners in 2016, following a successful career as a Partner and Portfolio Manager at Heartland Advisors, where he co-managed a multi-billion-dollar small-cap value mutual fund. He currently serves on the board of the Coral Gables Trust Company and the Milwaukee Repertory Theater as board president. Adam earned a B.S. in International Relations with a focus on Environmental Sciences at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He continued his studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison where he earned an MBA through the Applied Security Analysis Program. Adam is a CFA® charter holder and a member of the CFA Institute since 2004.

members.name: Julie Purser
members.position: Managing Vice President, Customer Group Strategy
members.bio: Julie Purser is the Managing Vice President, Customer Group Strategy at Marriott International, based in Bethesda, Maryland. In her role, she leads enterprise-wide customer strategy and is focused on creating exceptional guest experiences that drive lifelong loyalty and in turn deliver value to Marriott’s business, franchisees and owners. Julie has previously held leadership roles at Marriott in Digital Products, Loyalty, Marketing, Partnerships and Credit Cards in the US and Asia Pacific.  Prior to Marriott, Julie was a partner at the global strategy consultancy, Prophet. She is currently based in Potomac, Maryland with her husband and two children. An animal lover and avid tennis player she loves to spend her time outdoors and traveling when she’s not at work!

members.name: Alan Rudikoff
members.bio: Alan Rudikoff is a co-founder and Partner of GDS Development Management LLC, a NYC based real estate development firm, with a focus on real estate finance and deal structuring for development projects. Alan has 30 years of experience in the real estate industry in both the United States and Europe. He worked for 10 years with Howard Ronson and the HRO Group in Paris, where he completed $5.1 billion in commercial real estate projects and sales in Paris, London and Frankfurt.In between HRO and GDS, Alan lived and worked in Stockholm for 7-years. Besides engaging in the Stockholm Waterfront Development as a personal Owner Developer with private equity capital, Alan later became a co-owner of a real estate development and fund management company with the main role as Director of Developments in addition to being a key member of the Transaction Group. This company raised two funds while Alan was still with the firm with a combined equity of circa $800 million raised from a handful of institutional pension funds.Prior to moving to Paris with HRO in 1996, Alan worked in the consulting group at E&Y Kenneth Leventhal Company. He graduated from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1991 with a BBA, and double major in Real Estate, and, Finance, Investments and Banking.

members.name: Ellen Sexton
members.position: Executive Vice President, Markets and Chief Growth Officer
members.bio: Ellen Sexton is an accomplished executive across health care, manufacturing, and airline industries. Ellen’s leadership has a proven record of delivering growth, driving organizational transformation, and developing high performing businesses. She currently serves as Executive Vice President, Markets and Chief Growth Officer at Blue Shield of California overseeing growth and performance for commercial and consumer markets with 6 million members. Previously, Ellen was the Chief Operating Officer of Curative, a leading healthcare services company that launched the first of its kind employer-based health insurance plan. Prior to this role, as Chief Operating Officer of Humana’s Group business, Ellen led the growth platform for 15 million medical, dental, vision and life members. Ellen also served as the CEO for the UnitedHealthcare Wisconsin Medicaid Health plan, gaining recognition for clinical innovation resulting in market leading quality. Within UnitedHealthcare’s Medicare business, Ellen successfully transitioned state and employer group retiree healthcare programs and launched UnitedHealthcare’s Part D prescription drug program enrolling 5 million members. Ellen is highly collaborative and forward thinking as a Board Member with a wide range of service across the Milwaukee Public Library Foundation Board, healthcare start-up advisory roles and an appointment on the WI Governor’s Health Equity Council. Ellen has a Bachelor of Business Administration from the University of Wisconsin and a Master of Business Administration from the University of Pittsburgh.

members.name: Steve Voskuil
members.bio:
Steve Voskuil is Senior Vice President & Chief Financial Officer for The Hershey Company (HSY). In this role, he serves as strategic partner to the CEO with responsibility for financial planning, capital allocation, profitable growth investment, tech-enabled cost optimization, controllership, and investor relations.

Steve joined Hershey in 2019 from Avanos Medical (AVNS, previously “Halyard Health”), a global medical supplies and device company serving healthcare needs in more than 90 countries. He served as the company’s Senior Vice President & Chief Financial Officer for five years after leading its successful spinoff from Kimberly-Clark as a public company.

Before Halyard Health Inc., Steve worked for 23 years at Kimberly-Clark Corporation (KMB), a Fortune 150 global consumer products company. During this time, he gained financial and operational management experience across a variety of global senior leadership roles.

Steve is a member of the Board of Directors for Bath & Body Works where he chairs the Audit Committee and serves on the Human Capital and Compensation Committee. Steve also serves as the Vice Chair of the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia’s Economic and Community Advisory Council.

Steve has a bachelor’s degree from University of Wisconsin, Madison and a master’s degree from the Stanford Graduate School of Business, Palo Alto.

Steve and Colette live in Hershey and travel regularly to Texas and Wisconsin to spend time with their three sons and two granddaughters.

members.name: Kelly Weight
members.bio:
Kelly Weight is the visionary co-founder and CEO of Brillect, a women-owned consulting firm specializing in finance, accounting, digital and human resources solutions. With a career comprised of leadership roles at Target, Microsoft, and Salo, Kelly brings decades of experience and a deep understanding of the corporate world to her entrepreneurial journey.

Driven by a passion for people and a belief that business success stems from taking care of others, Kelly co-founded Brillect in 2021. Under her leadership, Brillect has grown into a $25+ million firm with over 150 employees, with offices in the Twin Cities and Milwaukee.

Kelly’s leadership is defined by her deep empathy and unwavering optimism. She has a unique ability to see possibilities where others might see obstacles, and she approaches challenges not as setbacks, but as opportunities for growth and connection. Her willingness to step into the unknown, take bold risks, and lead with vulnerability has been instrumental in Brillect’s success. Kelly leads with heart and a clear vision: that when people are cared for, they thrive, and so does the business.

A graduate of the University of Wisconsin–Madison with a BBA in accounting, Kelly began her career at Arthur Andersen before transitioning into compliance, audit, and project management roles. Her journey eventually led her to Microsoft, where she served as an Account Executive before launching Brillect.

Beyond her professional achievements, Kelly is deeply committed to community service. She mentors students through Minnetonka High School’s VANTAGE program, supports nonprofits like Feed My Starving Children and Way to Grow Minneapolis, and has served on the board of Spay and Neuter Kansas City. Under her guidance, Brillect donates a portion of its net income annually to organizations such as St. Jude’s, Junior Achievement, and the National MS Society.

Kelly is also a frequent speaker and panelist at industry events, sharing her insights on leadership, entrepreneurship, and work-life integration. A proud hockey mom of three boys, dog lover, and avid runner, Kelly leads with heart, purpose, and an unwavering commitment to helping others thrive.

members.name: Brad Zastoupil
members.bio: Brad Zastoupil is an audit partner at PwC in Minneapolis. Brad has extensive experience serving mid and large-cap domestic and multi-national public companies in multiple sectors.Outside of work, Brad serves on the Board of Directors and Audit Committee for BestPrep (Minnesota-based non-profit that prepares students with business, career and financial literacy skills), is an Advisory Board Member for the University of Wisconsin accounting department, and is PwC’s lead partner for recruiting activities at the University of Wisconsin.

members.name: Paul Collins
members.bio:
Paul Collins of London, England, is a retired vice chairman of Citigroup. He joined Citicorp in 1961 and worked in various executive positions including chief investment officer, with responsibility for Europe, Middle East, and Africa, and chief financial officer. In 1985, Collins was appointed a director of Citicorp and its principal subsidiary, Citibank, and in 1988, he became vice-chairman. He is a director of BG Group, Actis Capital LLP, and The Enstar Group, and was previously a director of Nokia and Kimberly-Clark.

Collins serves on the University of Wisconsin Foundation Board of Directors and was the co-chair of the university’s Create the Future capital campaign. He is a former member of the Wisconsin School of Business Dean’s Advisory Board and has received the Wisconsin School of Business Distinguished Alumnus Award and Wisconsin Alumni Association’s Distinguished Alumnus Award. In 2001, Collins made a gift in honor of his mother, Adele Stoppenbach Collins, to endow 16 School of Music graduate fellowships in the College of Letters and Science, and has endowed two School of Music professorships.

members.name: Phill Gross
members.bio:
Phill is a Co-Founder and Managing Director of Adage Capital Management, a Boston-based Money Management firm focused on managing S&P 500 assets, predominantly for Endowments and Foundations such as Harvard University, Northwestern University, Dartmouth College, the American Red Cross and the Getty Foundation.

Prior to founding Adage, Phill was a Healthcare and Retail analyst, equity research director and partner at the Harvard Management Company for 18 years after graduating from the University of Wisconsin with an MS in finance in 1983 and a BS in finance and economics in 1982.

Other Affiliations/Boards:

UW Foundation / UW Foundation Investment CommitteeSteve Hawk Center for Applied Securities Analysis Advisory BoardShelter, Inc. Strategic Advisory Council, ChairShelter, Inc. Board of Directors 1998-2006Strategic Grant Partners, Founder and Treasurer

members.name: Jon D. Hammes
members.bio:
Jon Hammes is the Managing Partner of Hammes Company. His primary responsibilities include providing overall leadership and managing the efforts of the national organization. Hammes Company is in the development, financing and management of strategic real estate assets, specifically in the healthcare and sports industry. Hammes Partners, is a registered institutional private equity fund that develops and acquires healthcare facilities on behalf of pension funds, endowments and foundations nationally.

Jon has been an active participant in the Milwaukee community. He serves on the boards of the Medical College of Wisconsin, the University of Wisconsin Foundation, Marquette University, Summerfest and Teach for America. In addition, he serves on the boards of the Greater Milwaukee Committee, the Milwaukee Metropolitan Association of Commerce, the Badger Institute, and WiCab Inc.

Jon earned an M.S. degree in Real Estate and Urban Land Economics from the University of Wisconsin and a BBA degree from the University Wisconsin-Milwaukee.

members.name: Ted D. Kellner
members.bio:
BBA 1969Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Fiduciary ManagementMequon, Wis.

Ted D. Kellner is chairman and chief executive officer of Fiduciary Management, Inc. of Milwaukee, Wis. He is a Chartered Financial Analyst with more than 39 years of investment experience, and a founder and portfolio manager for Fiduciary Management, Inc., an investment management firm established in 1980. The firm currently manages more than $5 billion in assets. Kellner also founded and serves as a director and treasurer of Fiduciary Real Estate Development, Inc., which owns more than 3,500 multi-family units in the state of Wisconsin. Kellner serves on the boards of American Family Mutual Insurance Company, Lakeview Equity Partners, Marshall & Illsley, Metavante Corporation, and Mason Wells, Inc.

In the non-profit arena, Kellner has served on the board of Milwaukee-area organizations, including the Children’s Hospital System, the Greater Milwaukee Committee, the Medical College of Wisconsin, Milwaukee World Festival, Inc., and the United Way of Greater Milwaukee.

Kellner and his wife, Mary, BSE 1968, have been generous contributors to UW-Madison. Kellner has held many top volunteer posts, including chairman of the board of the University of Wisconsin Foundation, president of the Wisconsin Alumni Association and president of the Wisconsin School of Business Board of Visitors. In 1994, Kellner was awarded the Wisconsin Distinguished Business Alumnus Award from the business school and in 1998, he received the Distinguished Alumnus Award from the Wisconsin Alumni Association.

members.name: Mike Knetter
members.bio:
Albert O. Nicholas DeanWisconsin School of Business2002-2010

Michael M. Knetter joined the Wisconsin School of Business as its dean in July 2002. As dean, he has orchestrated the novel $85 million Wisconsin Naming Gift, the expansion of Grainger Hall, the restructuring and improved national standing of the full-time MBA, and the restructuring and expansion of the Enterprise MBA programs for working professionals.

Prior to joining the school, he was associate dean of the MBA program and professor of international economics in the Amos Tuck School of Business at Dartmouth College.

Knetter has published widely in the areas of international and macroeconomics. He served as senior staff economist for the President’s Council of Economic Advisors for former presidents George H.W. Bush and Bill Clinton, and is currently research associate for the National Bureau of Economic Research and faculty affiliate of the La Follette School of Public Affairs. He is a director of American Family Insurance and Wausau Paper, and a former director of Great Wolf Resorts. He also currently serves as a trustee of Neuberger Berman Funds and Northwestern Mutual Series Fund, and as a member of the Advisory Board of the newly formed Wisconsin Business Council. He is chairing the capital campaign for The Road Home of Dane County, a non-profit that assists in finding housing and work solutions for homeless families in Dane County.

In March 2010, Knetter was named UW-Madison’s vice chancellor for advancement, in addition to leading the business school. In October 2010, he took over as President and CEO of the University of Wisconsin Foundation. To commemorate Dean Michael Knetter’s leadership at the Wisconsin School of Business, over 200 alumni and friends joined together to make a collective gift of $5.4 million to the School of Business and make Knetter an honorary member of the Wisconsin Naming Partnership.

Knetter completed his undergraduate studies in economics and mathematics at the University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire and his Ph.D. in economics at Stanford University.

members.name: Paul Leff
members.bio: Paul runs his family office, Warbasse67, out of NYC. Previously, Paul co-founded Perry Capital in 1988 and served as CIO. He retired from Perry Capital at the end of 2014. From 1986 to 1988, Paul was a principal and portfolio manager of Harvard Management Company. From 1984 to 1986, he was a trader and research analyst at Kayne, Anderson and Co., where he specialized in corporate reorganizations. Paul is a founding member of the Wisconsin Naming Partners, a University of Wisconsin Foundation board member and the Co-Chairman of the Wisconsin Eastern Alumni Scholarship Fund, an organization providing academic scholarships to minority, disadvantaged students from New York City. He is also a member of the Board of Trustees of The Allen-Steven School in NYC. Paul has been an owner of the Oakland Raiders since 2007. He earned an MS in Finance in 1984, and a BBA in Finance and Economics in 1983 at the University of Wisconsin.

members.name: Sheldon B. Lubar
members.bio:
BBA 1951, JD 1953Founder & Chairman, Lubar & Co., Inc.River Hill, Wis.

Sheldon B. Lubar is founder and chairman of Lubar & Co., a Milwaukee-based private investment firm active in corporate acquisitions and venture capital investment. He formed Lubar & Company while also serving as chairman and CEO of Mortgage Associates (1966-1973) and president and chairman of the executive committee of Midland National Bank, (1975-1977), both of Milwaukee.

He served as assistant secretary of the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, commissioner of the Federal Housing Administration, director of the Federal National Mortgage Association and commissioner of the White House Conference on Small Business. He also served the state of Wisconsin on its Commission on Education, the Commerce and Industry Task Force and as a trustee of the state’s Investment Board. In 1991, he was appointed a regent of the University of Wisconsin, where he also served as system president. Lubar was named a Distinguished Alumnus by the Wisconsin School of Business.

In 2006, Lubar contributed $10 million to the UW-Milwaukee School of Business Administration, which was renamed the Sheldon B. Lubar School of Business in his honor.

members.name: John Morgridge
members.bio:
John Morgridge of Portola, Calif., is chairman emeritus of Cisco Systems Inc. He joined Cisco in 1988 as president and CEO, and grew the company from $5 million to more than $1 billion in sales, and from 34 to more than 2,250 employees. In 1990, he took Cisco public, in 1995 was appointed chairman, and in November, 2006 he became chairman emeritus. During his tenure, Cisco has become the worldwide leader in networking for the Internet, with more than $30 billion in annual revenues and some 54,500 employees in 77 countries.

Morgridge and his wife, Tashia, actively support a range of education, conservation, and human services initiatives. He serves on the boards of Business Executives for National Security, CARE, the Cisco Foundation, the Cisco Learning Institute, Interplast, the Nature Conservancy, TOSA Foundation, and the Wisconsin Alumni Research Foundation (WARF).

The Morgridges have a long and distinguished record of support to the Wisconsin School of Business and the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Evidence of their generosity can be seen throughout campus, from Morgridge Auditorium in Grainger Hall, to the lakefront, to the Red Gym, where the Morgridge Center for Public Service is now housed. In 2004, the couple gave the university $31 million to complete and renovate the Education Building. In April 2006, the Morgridges announced a $50 million gift to fund the building of the Wisconsin Institutes for Discovery.

Morgridge was awarded the Wisconsin Distinguished Business Alumnus Award in 1991 and served on the Wisconsin School of Business Dean’s Advisory Board from 1987-1991. He received an honorary doctorate degree from UW-Madison in 1994. The Morgridges were both awarded the Distinguished Alumni Award from the Wisconsin Alumni Association in 2005.

members.name: John J. Oros
members.bio:
Mr. Oros is an Operating Partner at J.C. Flowers & Co. Prior to being named an Operating Partner, Mr. Oros was a Managing Director of the firm from 2006-2018. Before joining J.C. Flowers, Mr. Oros held a number of executive positions at Enstar Group Limited, including the role of Executive Chairman from 2000 – 2010. Prior to that, Mr. Oros was an investment banker in the Financial Institutions Group of Goldman Sachs for almost 20 years, where he became a General Partner in 1986. In addition, Mr. Oros was appointed Chairman of the Federal Savings and Loan Council in 1987, where he served for two years.

Mr. Oros serves on the Board of Directors of Island Finance, Jefferson Capital and Fairstone Financial. Mr. Oros received a B.B.A. from the University of Wisconsin School of Business

Oros lives in Ridgewood, N.J., with his wife Anne, who graduated from the School of Social Work at UW-Madison in 1971. They have four children and have been foster parents to 26 newborn children through the New Jersey Department of Children and Families and several private agencies. Oros is an appointee to the New Jersey Task Force on Child Abuse and Neglect, a member of the Investment Committee of the Children’s Aid and Family Services of New Jersey and is chairman of the University of Wisconsin Foundation. Oros was an appointee as chairman of the Federal Savings and Loan Advisory Council and served 10 years on the Board of the Community Foundation of New Jersey. He is a Distinguished Eagle Scout and is a past president of the Ridgewood Glen-Rock Council of the Boy Scouts of America, a director of the Greater NY Council and served on the Northeast Region Board of the Boy Scouts of America.

In 2004, the Oros’ gave $1 million to the Wisconsin School of Business, naming the John J. and Anne W. Oros Dining Room and the Kenneth B. Wackman Courtyard at the Fluno Center for Executive Education on the UW-Madison campus and funding the John J. Oros MBA Speaker Series at the business school. John was named a Wisconsin Distinguished Business Alumnus in 1999.

members.name: H. Signe Ostby
members.bio:
I joined Procter & Gamble in 1976 as a Brand Assistant on a test market product, Comet Liquid. Giving trial size versions of new products to consumers was the most important promotion to launch new products, as it gave customers a chance to try the product without paying for it. At that time most of the trial sizes were delivered through the mail or hung on front doors by crews of people. As you can imagine, those introductions cost a huge amount of money! My first major project was to run a test of In-Store Sampling to determine the effectiveness of handing out trial sizes in the stores compared to the costs of the other delivery methods. It was a huge coordination effort with R&D, package design, manufacturing, market research, sales, distribution, and brand services. But it was a success! I became the “expert” within the company about this type of introduction and it was because of that experience that another brand management person, Scott Cook, contacted me about using this type of sampling for a new food product.

In addition to Comet Liquid, I worked on Dawn, Ivory Snow and Dreft while at Procter & Gamble. After three years there, I moved to California and joined the Clorox Company working on Clorox 2, Twice as Fresh, and a group of new products that were either developed internally at Clorox, licensed from a German company, or acquired from local sources. New products were the “sexy” products to be managing, but in the early 80’s, nothing compared to the hype around the new personal computer market. At that point, I decided to see if I could apply the concepts I learned managing consumer packaged goods products to the emerging high-tech marketplace. Despite the fact that I didn’t have a electronic engineering or computer science background, I talked my way into a brand-new start-up, Software Publishing Corporation, which made productivity software for personal computers.

One of the first products that I worked on was a new word processor under development. Working ’til all hours with the engineering team to make sure this product was designed for regular business people, we came up with some very innovative features. At the same time, we knew that Microsoft was developing their new word processor and would launch just after we were scheduled to ship ours. Knowing that getting potential customers to try our product and have them make the decision to buy before they saw the Microsoft product would be instrumental in our success, I turned to my old friend, the trial size. I worked with my product development team to come up with a way to disable some key features of the product, and put an easy to use “getting started” card in the envelope of the floppy disk. We gave thousands of copies to the retail stores, handed them out at trade shows, put 800 #’s in our advertising where people could call and request a sample. The trial-size promotion helped catapult pfs:write to the top of the non-secretarial market segment of the word processing category.

After leaving Software Publishing in 1988, I started my marketing strategy consulting practice and worked for many of the personal computer hardware and software companies, including: IBM, HP – printers and software, Apple, Epson, Egghead, Radio Shack, Compaq, and a wide variety of software companies. In addition, I developed a seminar series which taught consumer packaged goods concepts to high-tech companies selling their products through retail stores.

Guiding the marketing strategy of a complex, multi-product company is an evolutionary step from being the product manager of a single product. The wide range of skills I learned as a product manager have been instrumental in my entire career and helped me transition successfully from the disciplined consumer packaged goods market to the high-tech area.

members.name: Michael S. Shannon
members.bio:
Mr. Shannon co-founded KSL Capital Partners, LLC in 2004 and co-founded its predecessor KSL Recreation Corporation in 1992, serving as its President and Chief Executive Officer.

Since 2005, KSL Capital Partners has raised over $6.5 billion in equity capital commitments and invests exclusively in travel and leisure businesses.

Mr. Shannon co-founded and became Chief Executive Officer of KSL Resorts in 2004 following the sale of KSL Recreation. Prior to establishing KSL Recreation with Kohlberg Kravis Roberts, he served as President and CEO of Vail Associates, Inc. (owner of Vail and Beaver Creek Resorts) in Vail, Colorado, from 1986 to 1992.

He currently serves on the Board of Trustees of Northwestern University, and as a Board Member of the University of Wisconsin Foundation, the Vail Valley Foundation, the United States Ski and Snowboard Team Foundation, Eisenhower Medical Center and ClubCorp Holdings, Inc. and as the Chairman of the Board of Vail Health Services. He is a past Director of Safeway, Inc., ING Direct, Conseco, Inc., TCA Cable TV, Inc., Startek, Inc. and ING Americas Holdings. Mr. Shannon is a member of the World Presidents’ Organization.

He holds a Bachelor of Business and Administration from the University of Wisconsin and a Master of Management in Accounting and Finance from Northwestern University’s Kellogg School of Management.
